claims.statement: The frame buffer is `{ w, h, cells }` in row-major 1-based order, and a cell is either one visible byte, `nil` or `""`, which is what makes the blank tri-state (transparent vs literal space) expressible at all.

`to_lines` returns exactly `h` lines each exactly `w` bytes wide with trailing spaces kept: that equality is the single seam to the mod-side golden frames, so changing it changes every delivered frame digest.

`blit` never raises — out-of-bounds or negative offsets are clipped as a block — while a single-cell `put` out of range is `-RANGE`, because a block overlay stepping on an edge is not a caller bug but a single-cell overflow is.
The blank tri-state is asserted in both directions: `nil` and `""` do not overwrite while a literal `" "` does, and asserting only that `blit` does not raise would leave I3 untested.

The perf table carries two columns because the gate runs debug (`cargo run -q --example selftest`) while production runs release: absolute caps are set from the slow side, so a debug gate does not go red on every run.

The composition path deliberately loses to hand-written `out = out .. ch` at width 80 (1.64x debug / 1.30x release) and the threshold is 2x anyway: what it guards is the growth behaviour of the concatenation path, not a speed win at this width.

The mod-side smoke file pins the load surface, export list, error-code set and the nine `perf.textframe.*` key names, and it must exist because `--filter` applies to mod `tests/*.lua` and package `test/*.lua` at the same time.
The narration host face takes a single `String` line, so colour and attribute cells have no consumer; adding them to the package would be a host-surface change, not a package capability.
